newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC OK's Enova/Pacific Enterprises merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC OK's Enova/Pacific Enterprises merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday conditionally approved the planned merger of Enova Corp and Pacific Enterprises .

The commission said the merger raised concern about the market power that Southern California Gas Co would have over natural gas supplies to competitors of San Diego Gas and Electric Co when the two companies merged.
Southern California Gas Co is a subsidiary of Pacific Enterprises and San Diego Gas and Electric is a unit of Enova.

The commission said the two companies would need to set up codes of conduct to ensure that any competing electricity generators would have open access to natural gas transportation on Southern California Gas's system, but it would be up to the California Public Utilities Commission to ensure that the two companies put those measures in place.

"The bottom line here is while there may be concerns about vertical market power, we do go forward and acknowledge that the California commission has the jurisdiction to address those concerns," Commissioner Vicky Bailey said at the commission meeting.
The merger must now be approved by the California commission, which is expected to finish its review of the $5.2 billion merger before the end of the year.
